vars.coverSub: Today we confirm owners, the first sprint, what we need access to, and how we will know it is working.
vars.bigorangeTeam: Strategy and messaging lead. Project management and web production on the working team. Dillon Mohr on SEO, AI search and WordPress.
vars.clientTeam: Owner and decision maker. One reviewer for facts and images. One person who labels leads in the CRM.
vars.cadenceBody: A 30-minute working session every other week, a written update in between, and a monthly review with numbers.
vars.heardTitle: What you told us matters most
vars.heardIntro: From the proposal conversation and the intake call. Correct anything that is off.
heardBullets: The website does not explain who you build for or where.
Project photos exist but permissions are unclear.
Inquiries come in, then sit; nobody owns the follow-up.
You want to be found for custom home builder searches in your markets.
Reporting today stops at clicks and form fills.
scopeRows: Discovery, audit, keyword and content strategy, architecture, priorities
Priority page rebuild, two supporting articles, technical SEO, WordPress implementation
Project permissions, process facts, reviewer sign-off, CRM lead labels
vars.scopeTakeaway: Anything not on this table is a change request, and that is fine; we just write it down.
vars.measureBar: Search Console  +  GA4  +  verified form and call events  +  CRM source  +  your sales feedback

accessItems.title: WordPress
accessItems.body: Role-specific editor account or a revocable Application Password. Read-only first.

accessItems.title: GA4 and Tag Manager
accessItems.body: Viewer on GA4, read on GTM.

accessItems.title: CRM or inbox
accessItems.body: A way to see which leads sales accepted, and why.

accessItems.title: Brand and proof
accessItems.body: Logo files, approved photos, reviews we may quote, project permissions.

vars.first30Title: The first four weeks, week by week
vars.week1: Access confirmed, technical crawl, keyword baseline, proof inventory started.
vars.week2: Audit findings reviewed with you; priority page and article plan agreed.
vars.week3: Priority page drafted and staged privately; first article drafted.
vars.week4: Review and QA; release the priority page if approved; measurement baseline captured.
vars.first30Takeaway: By day 30 you have seen the audit, approved the plan, and reviewed the first page in staging.
decisions: Name your factual reviewer and release owner
Approve the proof we may use
Confirm who labels leads in the CRM
Set the biweekly session day and time
vars.closeBody: We will come back in two weeks with the audit findings, the priority page plan, and the first draft schedule.
